rationale: Block 3 covers clinical presentation of dysphagia including the key distinction between oropharyngeal and oesophageal types based on symptom timing.

Block 9 covers the diagnostic framework for dysphagia, including the critical clinical distinction between solid-only and solid-plus-liquid dysphagia for differentiating mechanical obstruction from motility disorders.
Block 5 covers examination and investigation of tonsillitis. The Centor/FeverPAIN score and the amoxicillin-EBV trap are high-stakes examination points.
Block 9 covers management including indications for tonsillectomy. The Paradise criteria are a key factual anchor.
Block 8 covers post-operative complications including secondary haemorrhage. The timing and clinical significance of secondary haemorrhage (day 5-10) is a high-stakes safe-practice point.
Block 4 covers instruments and principles of tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy — identifying the correct surgical instruments is a standard surgical anatomy question.
Block 4 covers pathophysiology of key oesophageal conditions. Understanding achalasia pathophysiology and differentiating oesophageal carcinoma subtypes are high-yield topics.
Block 9 covers management principles including the key clinical trap distinguishing squamous cell carcinoma versus adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus, which is a high-yield factual distinction.
